messages:
Maya: heads-up — we saw a big surge where lots of requests from us-east ended up being routed to eu-west and then bounced to v2-quant repeatedly, causing a thundering-herd on the quantized variant :eyes:
Jon: ugh, do we have a single place that shows the routing decision chain for these requests?
Maya: yes, pulled a snippet from the router logs: `route_id=rc-91a2 region=us-east preferred_region=us-east fallback_region=eu-west model_requested=gptx-large model_served=v2-quant decision=redirect reason=capacity_soft_limit backoff=0s` — note the backoff=0s
Li: backoff=0s + immediate redirect => everyone retries instantly and keeps hitting the same variant. that explains the spike.
Sam: can you paste the exact policy blob that led to backoff=0s? might be a rollout override?
Maya: here — trimmed policy: ```json
{"routing_policy":"tiered_preference","fallback":"variant_prefer","fallback_backoff_seconds":0,"cross_region_allowed":true}
```
Hannah: that fallback_backoff_seconds=0 is the killer. we had intended a jittered exponential backoff for cross-region fallbacks. looks like a mistake in the rollout config.
Jon: where did that rollout come from? devflow? console?
Maya: it was a canary change pushed via the new rollouts UX (PR #4123) yesterday — probably the default got set to 0 for quick failover testing.
Sam: short-term mitigation: add a circuit-breaker on the router that enforces per-customer fallback cooldown of ~5-15s and randomize by +-30% to avoid sync. I can push a rule in the router today. @Jon can you help with a hotfix?
Jon: on it. I'll add `fallback_cooldown_ms = rand(5000,15000)` at the routing layer and enable for canary traffic only to verify.
Li: also suggest we add a variant capacity scoreboard so routing can prefer underutilized variants rather than a fixed order. long term but will help.
Maya: agreed. Sam, can you also add a temporary dashboard panel: "fallbacks by variant and origin region" and a spike alert? Ops needs a 5-min alert threshold.
Sam: adding dashboard now. Query I plan to use: `sum by (origin_region, target_variant) (increase(router_fallback_count[5m]))`
Hannah: for the rollouts UX — can we change the default in the UI so fallback_backoff_seconds can't be 0 unless explicitly checked? add a tooltip explaining the thundering herd risk. I'll file a small UX change.
Maya: filing is great. Ticket: PLAT-1192 (will link after create).
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-PLAT-86, severity=high, assigned=eng-platform, created_by=Maya
deploy-bot: deploy started: router-hotfix-190100-jon (jon) -> staging
Jon: pushed hotfix to staging with fallback cooldown and jitter. running load-sim to validate. logs show fallback attempts spread out now.
Maya: load-sim looks much better. peak qps on v2-quant dropped 72%, overall latency improved. thank you. :thumbsup:
Sam: dashboard added and alert wired to #oncall. also added a quick table showing customers that experienced >100 fallbacks in 10m so we can reach out.
Li: noted for longer-term: we should update smart-routing to incorporate variant utilization and a probabilistic fallback that decays with retries. will sketch an RFC.
Hannah: UX ticket created: https://go.redwood/PLAT-1192 — default now set to 5s in the form and a confirmation required for 0s.
Maya: next steps: Jon to promote hotfix to prod after a quick canary, Sam to keep the alerting and dashboard, Li + I will draft the RFC for utilization-aware routing, Hannah will follow up on UX. please update PLAT-1192 with any follow-ups.
Jon: canary is green. promoting to prod in 5.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: router-hotfix-190100-jon -> prod (2026-03-18T18:21:10Z)
Maya: mitigation complete. will convert to a postmortem (short) once we have the graphs in the incident ticket. thanks all.
Maya: retrospective note: avoid defaults that opt-in to zero-backoff. we should make the rollouts UX and the routing policy validators explicit about hazards.
Hannah: adding a checklist item in release playbook: validate fallback_backoff_seconds > 0 for any cross-region-enabled policy.
Maya: assigning owners in the incident: Jon (hotfix + validation), Sam (dashboards + alerts), Li (RFC), Hannah (UX + release playbook).
Jon: I'll link the hotfix PR and the prod logs in the incident thread.
Maya: end — follow-up in INC-2026-PLAT-86 and PLAT-1192. thx.
